title: China races to build data centres in bid for AI supremacy
source_used: Financial Times, read through BigGo Finance (a relay that names the FT report of 8 Oct 2026)
key_facts: The Financial Times reported on 8 Oct 2026 that China is significantly expanding data centre construction in inland regions rich in energy resources (as relayed by BigGo).
Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia alone has 89 data centres either built or planned (as relayed by BigGo).
Ulanqab's advantages are cited as abundant wind and coal power, cheap land, a cold climate and fast facility construction (BigGo's summary).
The relay says China faces difficulties securing advanced AI semiconductors while it pursues a strategy to narrow the gap with the US (BigGo's framing).
The FT's own text could not be read; figures added by BigGo from other sources are not used in this entry.
quote_evidence: The Financial Times reported on the 8th that China is significantly expanding data center construction centered on inland regions rich in energy resources.
Ulanqab alone has 89 data centers either built or planned.
why_it_matters_hint: China is building AI data centre capacity at scale using cheap power and land, in a race with the US over AI infrastructure.
